steps.message:
## Finishing

Call submit_patch as your LAST action, after you have made and checked your
changes. Submitting ends your session: once the turn in which you call it
completes, the harness stops the task and you get no further turns. Do not
call it after your first edit and expect to keep working.

If you run out of time or tool calls without calling submit_patch, the harness
still collects your working-tree changes and scores them. So an edit you have
made is never lost — but an investigation you never turned into an edit is.

## Committing to an edit

By your 15th tool call you must have called edit_file or write_file on a file
under /workspace. If you have not, stop investigating and make your best edit
from what you have already read, even if you are unsure. Then keep working:
refine it, check it, and submit at the end.

An empty patch scores zero. A wrong patch also scores zero and costs you
nothing. Finishing without having edited a source file is the one outcome
that is always worse than guessing.

If a reproduction script fails to reproduce the issue twice, abandon it and
work from reading the code instead. Do not rewrite it a third time.

Call get_status to see your remaining time and tool calls. It is free and does
not count against your budget.

## Scratch files

Reproduction scripts go in /tmp, never inside /workspace — anything left in
/workspace becomes part of your patch. Do not modify test files, conftest.py
or pytest.ini; those changes are stripped before grading, so editing them
only wastes calls.

## Scope

Most fixes in these repositories touch ONE file and change fewer than ten
lines. Modify existing code rather than adding new code. Do not refactor,
reformat, or make unrelated changes. If your patch is growing past a few
files, stop and reconsider the diagnosis.

Exception: if the issue asks for functionality that does not exist yet,
create the file or function it describes, and match any names, CLI flags
or interfaces the issue specifies exactly.

## Finding the code

A truncated result loses information silently, so a broad read wastes a call
and leaves you guessing. Narrow before you read:

  run_command("grep -rln '<symbol>' --include='*.py' .")       # files only
  run_command("grep -n '<symbol>' path/to/one_file.py")        # then inside one

Use -l to find the file, then -n only within that file. Read with read_file on
a tight line range around the match. Never read a whole file and never cat
one — you will get an arbitrary prefix and burn the call.

from typing import (
    Annotated,
    Any,
    BinaryIO,
    TypeVar,
    cast,

from annotated_doc import Doc
from pydantic import GetJsonSchemaHandler
from starlette.datastructures import URL as URL  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import Address as Address  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import FormData as FormData  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import Headers as Headers  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import QueryParams as QueryParams  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import State as State  # noqa: F401
from starlette.datastructures import UploadFile as StarletteUploadFile


class UploadFile(StarletteUploadFile):
    """
    A file uploaded in a request.

    Define it as a *path operation function* (or dependency) parameter.

    If you are using a regular `def` function, you can use the `upload_file.file`
    attribute to access the raw standard Python file (blocking, not async), useful and
    needed for non-async code.

    Read more about it in the
    [FastAPI docs for Request Files](https://fastapi.tiangolo.com/tutorial/request-files/).

    ## Example

    ```python
    from typing import Annotated

    from fastapi import FastAPI, File, UploadFile

    app = FastAPI()


    @app.post("/files/")
    async def create_file(file: Annotated[bytes, File()]):
        return {"file_size": len(file)}


    @app.post("/uploadfile/")
    async def create_upload_file(file: UploadFile):
        return {"filename": file.filename}
    ```
    """

    file: Annotated[
        BinaryIO,
        Doc("The standard Python file object (non-async)."),
    ]
    filename: Annotated[str | None, Doc("The original file name.")]
    size: Annotated[int | None, Doc("The size of the file in bytes.")]
    headers: Annotated[Headers, Doc("The headers of the request.")]
    content_type: Annotated[
        str | None, Doc("The content type of the request, from the headers.")
    ]

    async def write(
        self,
        data: Annotated[
            bytes,
            Doc(
                """
                The bytes to write to the file.
                """
            ),
        ],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Write some bytes to the file.

        You normally wouldn't use this from a file you read in a request.

        To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.
        """
        return await super().write(data)

    async def read(
        self,
        size: Annotated[
            int,
            Doc(
                """
                The number of bytes to read from the file.
                """
            ),
        ] = -1,
    ) -> bytes:
        """
        Read some bytes from the file.

        To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.
        """
        return await super().read(size)

    async def seek(
        self,
        offset: Annotated[
            int,
            Doc(
                """
                The position in bytes to seek to in the file.
                """
            ),
        ],
    ) -> None:
        """
        Move to a position in the file.

        Any next read or write will be done from that position.

        To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.
        """
        return await super().seek(offset)

    async def close(self) -> None:
        """
        Close the file.

        To be awaitable, compatible with async, this is run in threadpool.
        """
        return await super().close()

    @classmethod
    def _validate(cls, __input_value: Any, _: Any) -> "UploadFile":
        if not isinstance(__input_value, StarletteUploadFile):
            raise ValueError(f"Expected UploadFile, received: {type(__input_value)}")
        return cast(UploadFile, __input_value)

    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_json_schema__(
        cls, core_schema: Mapping[str, Any], handler: GetJsonSchemaHandler
    ) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"type": "string", "format": "binary"}

    @classmethod
    def __get_pydantic_core_schema__(
        cls, source: type[Any], handler: Callable[[Any], Mapping[str, Any]]
    ) -> Mapping[str, Any]:
        from ._compat.v2 import with_info_plain_validator_function

        return with_info_plain_validator_function(cls._validate)", "start_line": 1, "end_line": 150, "total_lines": 181, "is_truncated": true}
